title: ClassifiedErrorOutput
description: The envelope discriminated by `type: "error"`: a classified failure with the detail nested under `error`. Published in v1.0.4, when the discriminator table was first checked against the schemas and the entry for `error` turned out to point at `error-response.schema.json` — a DIFFERENT shape, where `error` is a plain string. An agent following the published routing would validate this document against that contract and see the whole thing rejected on the first keyword. Two emit sites: `run.rs` writes it to STDERR when argument parsing fails and stdout is not a TTY, and `commands::schema_cmd` writes it to STDOUT when `schema --name` is given an id the catalog does not ship. English-only: these are usage diagnostics, not search-result fields.

category.description: usage when the invocation itself is malformed; validation when the arguments parse but name something that does not exist.

code.description: Stable machine-readable identifier, e.g. invalid_config or unknown_schema. Left open: codes are additive and an agent branches on the exact string.

message.description: Human-readable explanation. Localized by the UI locale; never parse it.

retryable.description: Present when the emit site can classify retryability. Absent means unknown, never false.

known.description: Emitted by `schema --name` on an unknown id: the exact set of ids the catalog ships, so the agent can correct itself without a second round trip.
